text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Investment fund VUB Kupon, created during the first wave of voucher privatisation, will pay an after-tax dividend of 10 crowns per share.

- The Slovak government will discuss at its regular Tuesday session a draft law against excessive imports of goods that are also produced in Slovakia. No other major economic items are on the government's preliminary agenda.
- Slovak construction output totalled 61.6 billion crowns in 1996 and accounted for around 4.7 percent of the entire gross domestic product.
- The National Bank of Slovakia said measures implemented in 1996 were successful in those economic spheres which are under the NBS influence.

PRAVDA - Printing company Perex a.s. on Monday completed distribution of 4.5 million ballots for the forthcoming referendums. The ballots have four questions - three questions related to NATO membership and one question on direct presidential elections.

- U.S ambassador to Slovakia, Ralph Johnson, said Washington would respect any Slovak decision to declare military neutrality but added that Bratislava cannot expect the U.S. to guarantee its neutral state.

- The Confederation of Trade Unions said it would stick to its demand for the so-called 13th salary in 1997 even if this meant that the three parties in the social dialogue - the government, trade unions and the employers' association - will not sign a collective agreement for this year.
- The average income per one member of a family totalled 3,922 crowns in 1996 which is a decline of 30 percent in real terms against the year 1989.

SME - President Michal Kovac was reported as saying he did not intend to submit his candidacy in 1998 presidential elections even if the up coming referendum installed a direct citizen vote of the president.
- Kovac said he expected suffcient turnout and positive result at the referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections, both scheduled for next weekend.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said Slovakia would abolish the import deposit measure before the required date of June 5, but only on the condition that the Czech Republic would scrap its similar import deposits by May 29, as required by the EU.
- Slovakia's production of cement totalled 2.805 million tonnes in 1996, some 82,000 tonnes less than in 1995, which accounted for around 65 percent of the entire production capacity.
